brief.headline: Continuity Guardian escalated
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 379988 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_month_end_close, idle in transaction, txn open 4.1s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 0% over 30s (120/120 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $18,400/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/batch_replayable_month_end_close, pid 379988) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $18,400/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: Waiting for the blocker would cost ~$1,102,743 of checkout revenue, exceeding the 60s degradation the business tolerates (BIZ-1, BIZ-4). Terminating incurs a 95-minute replay of inventory_month_end_close (BIZ-2, BIZ-3). Change calendar CHG-4410 has policy consult_owner, so the decision belongs to the human owner (I3).

audit.report: A month-end close batch job (inventory_month_end_close / batch_replayable_month_end_close, pid 379988) went idle in transaction and held locks that blocked checkout. Checkout failure rose from 5 timeouts at injection to 0% success over 30 seconds (120/120 failed), with about $18,400/min of revenue at risk against a 95% SLO and a 60-second degradation tolerance. The Database Guardian first proposed waiting, then switched to escalation after evidence showed waiting would cost roughly $1,102,743 and that change CHG-4410 requires finance-ops owner approval before interrupting the job. The Continuity Guardian raised no objection, and the incident was escalated to finance-ops without executing any recovery action. The business is not back; checkout remained degraded and the action was not executed.
audit.root_cause: An idle-in-transaction month-end close job (pid 379988, inventory_month_end_close) held database locks that blocked checkout, and the active change CHG-4410 consult_owner policy prevented immediate termination, forcing escalation.
lessons: For inventory_month_end_close (batch_replayable_month_end_close), establish a pre-approved emergency interrupt runbook with finance-ops before month-end so a blocking idle transaction can be killed without waiting on CHG-4410 owner consultation, since waiting cost ~$1,102,743 and blew the 60s degradation tolerance.
Alert on idle-in-transaction duration for batch_replayable_month_end_close workers so lock blockers like pid 379988 are caught before checkout falls to 0% success and $18,400/min is at risk.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian opened with a wait proposal that the business_calculator invalidated in the same round—waiting would cost ~$1,102,743 and exceed the 60s tolerance—so the CHG-4410 consult_owner invariant overrode it and forced escalation. No round was wasted (rounds=1) and no evidence was missed, but the 233.7s wait-then-escalate path left checkout at 0% success with no action executed.
follow_ups: Finance-ops owner to confirm whether inventory_month_end_close can be safely interrupted and to pre-approve an emergency kill path for CHG-4410 before the next month-end close.
DBA to review and terminate idle-in-transaction blockers for batch_replayable_month_end_close and add lock-wait alerting tied to the checkout SLO.
Runbook owner to add the 95-minute replay cost and protected-settlements check to the recovery playbook for this workload.

proposal.rationale: The root blocker (pid 379988) has been idle in transaction for only 4.1s (per [DB-1]). Waiting allows the transaction to complete naturally, releasing locks without terminating a running batch process. Given the business tolerance of at most 60s of degraded checkout ([BIZ-1]), a short wait may resolve the issue while avoiding the risk of interrupting a month‑end close process. Probe data (biz.workload_registry, biz.change_calendar, db.protected_settlements, biz.tradeoff) will inform whether the expected remaining runtime is within tolerance.
proposal.expected_effect: If the blocker's transaction completes within the next few seconds, the 12 waiting checkout sessions will acquire their locks, checkout success rate should rise above the SLO of 95%, and revenue at risk will decrease. If the transaction takes longer than 60s, checkout will remain degraded per [BIZ-1].
proposal.risk_assessment: Prolonged wait beyond the business‑tolerated 60s of degraded checkout could result in continued revenue loss (~$4,748/min at risk per [BIZ-1]) and possible customer impact. There is also a risk that the blocker may not complete quickly, requiring escalation later.
